archetype.add_remove: O(components held), with a copy of the whole entity

axis_sorted.insert_remove_move: O(1), plus a deferred O(n log n)
axis_sorted.query_radius: O(log n + entities in the slab)

bitset_soa.create: amortised O(1), plus one word appended to each of five planes per 64 new slots

cell_rows.insert_remove_move: O(1), plus a deferred O(ids + cells) rebuild
cell_rows.query_knn: O(entities within the smallest sufficient box)

grid_undo_log.rewind: O(records in the discarded ticks), each costing a remove and an insert

grouped_sparse_set.create: amortised O(components in mask), plus two swaps when the mask holds both of the pair
grouped_sparse_set.destroy: O(components held), plus two swaps when the entity is a group member

morton_lbvh.query_knn: O(internal nodes expanded, one eight-box test and up to eight frontier pushes of O(log frontier) each + leaves expanded, sixteen entity tests each and an O(log k) heap update per entity kept)
morton_lbvh.query_radius: O(internal nodes whose box meets the sphere, one eight-box test each + leaves whose box meets the sphere, sixteen entity tests each); output-sensitive, with no worst-case bound below O(n)

morton_sorted.insert_remove_move: O(1), plus a deferred O(n log n)
morton_sorted.query_radius: O(cells touched * log n + entities in them)

reference.get_set: O(1) expected, with a dependent chain of loads

sparse_set.query: O(size of the smallest matching set)

spatial_hash.query_radius: O(cells touched probes + entities in them)

uniform_grid.query_knn: O(entities within the smallest sufficient box)

ecs_mixed.checks: nothing directly; it is the curve a game would actually see
ecs_mixed.measures: The same operation mix with integrate and one query per frame left on: the realistic shape of a frame rather than an isolated operation. Its exponent is expected to sit between the point-operation family's and 1, because a frame is a fixed number of operations plus two linear passes.

ecs_point_ops.checks: the `get_set` and `add_remove` lines of each ECS manifest
ecs_point_ops.measures: A fixed number of point operations per frame — get, set, add, remove, create, destroy — with integrate and the per-frame query switched off. Both of those are a full pass over the population, so leaving either on would make every candidate measure the pass rather than the operation.

rewind_depth.checks: no manifest field; it is the second axis of the history trade, against which a log's cost grows and a rebuild's does not
rewind_depth.measures: Two history strategies against how far back a rewind goes, at 10% of entities moving each tick. The median tick does not rewind and should not move with depth for either strategy. The median rewind tick is the median of the 9 ticks that open with a rewind, and is where a log that unwinds tick by tick and a rebuild that does not are expected to part as the depth grows. The p99 is the fifth costliest of the 399 ticks after the load tick: where every rewind costs more than any ordinary tick it is about the middle of the rewinds, and where a strategy's rewind costs about what an ordinary tick does, as a log's may at shallow depth, it is the tick tail rather than the rewind.

rewind_move_fraction.checks: no manifest field; it locates where the history strategies change order between the two points hs01 and hs02 measure
rewind_move_fraction.measures: Two history strategies against the share of entities that move each tick, with the rollback schedule fixed. The median tick does not rewind: it is the cost of keeping history while the world moves. The median rewind tick is taken over the 9 ticks that open with a rewind and nothing else, so it is the cost of putting the world back. The p99 tick is taken over the 99 ticks after the load tick, which the harness reports apart; it is the second costliest of them, so where every rewind costs more than any ordinary tick it is the second costliest rewind, and where a strategy's rewind costs about what an ordinary tick does, as a log's may when little moves, it is the tick tail and says nothing about the rewind.

spatial_knn.checks: the `query_knn` line of each spatial manifest's complexity field
spatial_knn.measures: One k-nearest query against a settled index. Separate from the radius family because a k-nearest query has to widen its search until it can prove it has the k closest, and that loop is where two candidates lost to a linear scan in the main suite.

spatial_move.checks: the `insert_remove_move` line of each spatial manifest's complexity field
spatial_move.measures: The cost of keeping the structure current under a fixed number of moves per tick. One radius query per tick is included on purpose: a candidate that rebuilds lazily does its work on the first observation, so with no query at all its rebuild would never happen and the family would measure an array write.

spatial_query_radius.checks: the `query_radius` line of each spatial manifest's complexity field
spatial_query_radius.measures: One radius query against a settled index. Nothing moves after the load tick, so no candidate is paying to keep itself current and this is the query path alone.

regimes.fixed_density: The world grows as the cube root of the population, so density and the size of a query's answer stay constant. The exponent measured here is the cost of finding the answer, which is what a complexity claim is about.
regimes.fixed_world: The world stays the same size, so density grows with the population and a query of fixed radius returns proportionally more entities. The exponent measured here includes the growth of the answer, not just the growth of the search.
regimes.population: Population grows with the operation count per frame held fixed. The only regime for a track with no world.
